head: 5,127 prototypes.
One vacuum.
slides.sub: How one engineer took on an industry that made money from bags.

image.label: A shed full of transparent vacuum prototypes
image.brief: 투명한 청소기 시제품 수십 개가 선반에 줄지어 있는 작업 창고. 작업등 하나, 늦은 밤.

head: The bag was
the problem.
body: In 1978, James Dyson noticed his vacuum cleaner kept losing suction. Dust clogged the pores of the bag, and the machine weakened long before the bag was full.

image.label: A clogged vacuum bag, dust everywhere
image.brief: 먼지로 막힌 청소기 먼지봉투 클로즈업. 회색 먼지가 날리는 장면.

head: The answer was
in a sawmill.
body: He had seen a cyclone tower at a sawmill spin sawdust out of the air, with no filter to clog.
Could a tiny cyclone do the same job inside a vacuum?

image.label: A tall industrial cyclone tower at a sawmill
image.brief: 제재소의 높은 원뿔형 사이클론 탑. 톱밥이 소용돌이치는 장면.

slides.label: prototypes over about five years
body: He built, tested and changed one thing at a time. Each failure taught him something the last one couldn’t. Money ran short and debts piled up.

image.label: Hundreds of numbered prototypes
image.brief: 번호표가 붙은 시제품 수백 개를 위에서 내려다본 구도.

head: It worked.
No one wanted it.
body: Big vacuum makers turned the design down. One reason was simple: they earned steady money selling replacement bags.
A vacuum with no bag would quietly kill that business.

image.label: A stack of replacement bags on a store shelf
image.brief: 매장 선반에 높이 쌓인 교체용 먼지봉투 상자들. 브랜드 없음.

head: Your idea works.
No one will make it.
body: You’re deep in debt. Every manufacturer at home has said no. What now?

options.feedback: He tried this for years. It wasn’t working. Keep swiping.

options.text: License the design abroad and use the money to keep going
options.feedback: This is what Dyson did. Keep swiping.

options.text: Sell the patents and move on
options.feedback: The safest choice. But the biggest payoff from the idea would go to someone else.

image.label: A lone inventor with a prototype, facing a closed office door
image.brief: 시제품을 든 발명가가 닫힌 회의실 문 앞에 서 있는 장면.

head: The first one sold
in Japan.
body: In 1986, a Japanese company launched his design as the G-Force, a high-end pink vacuum.
The licensing income helped him protect his patents and, in time, build a company of his own.

image.label: A pink 1980s vacuum in a Tokyo showroom
image.brief: 1980년대 도쿄 쇼룸의 분홍색 청소기. 실제 제품 디자인을 그대로 따라 하지 않음.

head: the DC01.
body: Dyson launched his own vacuum in Britain, with a clear bin so you could see the dirt. His ads made the bag the villain: “Say goodbye to the bag.”
Within about two years, it was reportedly the best-selling vacuum in the UK.

image.label: A see-through vacuum bin full of dust

head: Their profit was
his opening.
body: Rivals earned money on the bag, so a bagless machine threatened their business model, not just their product. That’s why they didn’t build it.
And 5,127 prototypes is build, measure, learn in hardware: many small, cheap tests before one big bet.

image.label: A cyclone of dust forming a question mark
image.brief: 먼지 소용돌이가 그래픽처럼 형상을 이루는 이미지.

head: Look for what rivals
can’t afford to fix.
body: Sometimes the biggest opening is a problem the market leader profits from.
**Try it today:** what annoying cost do your customers pay again and again? Who earns money from it?

image.label: A single clear vacuum bin glowing
image.brief: 어두운 배경 위 빛나는 투명 먼지통 하나.

factChecks.note: 시제품 5,127개(1979~1984년)는 Dyson 회사와 James Dyson 본인이 여러 차례 밝힌 수치입니다. 공식 연혁으로 다시 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 5,127개 시제품 확인(Dyson 공식 자료).
제재소의 사이클론에서 아이디어를 얻었다는 이야기는 Dyson의 공식 이야기입니다. 그가 운영하던 공장의 분진 처리 장치와 연결해 설명하는 판본도 있어 카드에는 "a sawmill"로만 적었습니다.
일본 G-Force 출시(1986)와 분홍색 디자인은 Dyson 공식 자료 기준입니다. 가격 수치는 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] G-Force 출시 연도를 1983년으로 적은 자료가 있음. 1986년 일본 출시는 이번 검색에서 미확인.
DC01 출시(1993)와 "약 2년 안에 영국 판매 1위"는 회사 발표에 근거합니다. 카드에는 "reportedly"를 붙였습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1993년 DC01, 2년 안에 영국 판매 1위 보도 확인(단일 출처).
기존 제조사가 교체용 먼지봉투 수익 때문에 라이선스를 거절했다는 설명은 Dyson 본인의 설명에 근거합니다. 회사별 거절 이유는 밝혀지지 않았으므로 "one reason"으로 표현했습니다.
광고 문구 "Say goodbye to the bag"은 Dyson 광고 캠페인 문구입니다. 사용 연도는 확인하세요.
